en: Understood!
Wha⑬how? I can't even shut down a long-retired batter!?
It's even harder to take on an active pro. You need to face reality.
So this is the world of the pros... It's... so harsh. Was I foolish to think I could measure up?
I wouldn't call it foolish. It's hard to say it's wrong to follow a dream.
But at the same time, what if you following your dream is hurting those who are important to you? Does that seem right to you?
Your sister is clearly worried about you. Aren't there ways of making her happy that don't involve pro baseball?
Come on, Kyuma. Let's go home. It's all right if you don't become a pro. There's happiness to be found in living a plain and simple life...
I can't!!!
I can't give up on my dreams! Please, give me one more chance, Shinada-san. Just one more, that's all I ask!
Okay. I'm gonna redouble my training and challenge you again. But next time, I'm shutting you down! This is the only thing that matters!
Geez! Don't you get it? I'll tell you flat out⑬you're never gonna make it to the pros!
Like hell I'm not! You'll be going down flailing next time!
Kyuma, wait! What about your thanks for roping Shinada-san into your ludicrous challenge?
Can't you see I'm busy? You deal with it. I need to go train!
*sigh* I'm so sorry. This isn't so much a thanks as it is a token of apology for all the trouble we put you through.
You got a <Color:8>Sturdy Knife<Color:Default>.
Please use it responsibly. Anyway, I'll talk some sense into Kyuma so he won't bother you again.
(I doubt he'll listen to reason. When he comes to challenge me again, I'll have to burst his bubble for good.)
(Dang. I underestimated the guy.)
I won. But why does this feel... so empty?
Did you let me win out of pity? I can't think of any other reason someone like you would bat like that.
Well that doesn't help my confidence any. I'll be waiting for a rematch. But next time, please don't pull your punches.
(Dangit!)
I've been waiting for you, Shinada-san. Please put in a proper effort this time.
I can't wait to show you what I gained from all my wilderness training!
Fine. If you lose this time, you're giving up your pro dream like you promised.
I agreed to it, and I honor my promises. Not that I'm about to lose.
Shinada-san! Oh, thank goodness.
You're... Kyuma-kun's older sister, right?
Yes, it's Akiyo. Listen, about my brother... He hasn't come home since that day.
He said he was going to try again, so I thought he would have come to see you, but I guess not.
No, I haven't seen him. But when I do, I'll make sure he gets his act together.
To be honest, I don't care if he keeps on dreaming. I'm only afraid that he might have hurt himself from training too hard.
Even if his dream can't come true, as long as he's safe, that's enough for me.
But... won't that only make things harder for you?
Oh, I'm quite used to that by now, haha. Well, I'll just have to keep looking for him, then.
Kyuma-kun! What's with you, man? Your sister's worried about you.
All that matters is our challenge, Shinada-san. I'm ready for you now.
I went off into the wilderness to train, and I finally developed the pitching to take you down. This time, you're mine!
All right. But you have to promise me something.
And what kind of promise would that be?
If you lose today, you give up your dream of turning pro.
If you can't make that promise, I won't accept your challenge. Is that what you want?
Fine. I'm a man of my word, after all. There's no way I'm going to lose!
See, look at that confidence right there. But, you asked for it. I'll show you what it really means to be a pro.
No! This is a nightmare! I trained over and over to perfect my pitching, and now...!

You promised. Today, you're going right back to that screw
factory and putting your elbow grease into where it's needed most.
One more! Please, you have to give me another shot. I'm sure I can win next time!
You said that last time! Just admit you lost and be done with it!
Urk...
Look, why do you want to be a pro so badly?
...It's the money, dammit! Can't you tell!?
Money? That's it?
Ever since our father died, we were always dirt poor.
Akiyo-chan practically raised me herself⑬she even skipped high school to do it! She sacrificed... everything for me.
I've been looking for a way to repay her ever since. To finally give her the good life she deserves.
But the only thing I have going for me is baseball. It's the only way I can earn big money.
And that's why you were so bent on becoming a pro.
Well, I can empathize with how you feel about your sister.
But in spite of your good intentions, you're only causing her grief. Are you aware of that?
I am. But if I were to turn pro⑬!
That's not the point. Akiyo-san isn't sad because you're poor, or because it's tough to keep the factory going.
It's because you're not hearing what she really wants you to hear.
You're... saying I'm ignoring my sister?
Have you ever asked her what her definition of a good life is? I'll bet my left nut you haven't.
...That's a no.
Way I see it, you want to be a pro baseball player, but you're using your sister to justify it.
You say it's for your sister's happiness⑬that way you can ignore reality and avoid giving up on your dream.
I'm not gonna tell you how to live your life. But you should seriously discuss your future with your sister.
Yes... I should. I will.
Kyuma! Thank goodness I found you!
Sis...

Look, I'm not mad or anything. But please... don't run off
without telling me. If something happened to you, I don't know what I'd do.
...I'm sorry, Akiyo-chan. For everything. I couldn't beat Shinada-san after all. So you know what? I'm done with baseball. For good.
(Good man.)
Are... Are you sure you're okay with that?
Yeah... You know what it was? I was afraid of admitting I didn't have the talent. I thought it'd be too painful.
But I'm gonna stop running from here on out. I have to face up to reality. After all, I'm too old not to.
Kyuma...
From now on, I'm listening carefully to everything you say. So, will you give me your excellent advice?
...I'd be glad to.
Shinada-san, thank you. I've decided to stop dreaming and start building. A future that's grounded on what I can do, not just some idea in my head.
And I'll make sure not to worry her again.
Good on you. And good luck!
Thanks! Oh, and please take this... for putting up with me.
You got a <Color:8>Kamaitachi Utility Knife<Color:Default>.
We'll be on our way now.
(Hope those two work together to make something truly great happen.)
(Dammit. Got too careless.)
I won. But why was it so easy? There was absolutely no substance to this.
Shinada-san, did you maybe let me win? Why else would someone like you bat like that?
That's no help to my confidence. I'll be waiting for a rematch. But next time, don't go easy on me, please.
(Dang!)
What, yer back for another shallenge? I like that! You got the fighting shpirit in you. *hic*
But I'm the only one feeling a little bit tipsy here and that's not fair, nuh-uh. Here, you got some catching up to do, you cheater!
...Well, I guess fair's fair.
Okay, I'll quit drinking if you can beat me. I'll throw five pitches! Hit one homer and you win. Got it, bucko?
Eh, why not. I really don't know why I'm doing this, other than I hate to lose. Man, must I have some serious pride issues...
Thassall I needed to hear! Let the duel commence! *hic*
Hey, buddy. You got time?
Oh, you mean me? Uh, I guess I do.
That's good. Good to know. Listen, you wanna tip back some sake with me?
Here? Now?

Yeah, why not? Nothing better than knocking back a lukewarm
cup of sake after working up a good sweat. Mm-mm!

But lemme tell ya, it's depressing to drink alone. Sharing
is caring, after all!
Huh. So you drink in the corner of a batting center... Well, I can see how it might feel relaxing after a workout.
You bet your bippy it does! Now I already got the sake, so it's all on me. Why don't you join me for a sip? You'll love it once you try it.
Really!? You're cool with that?
Darn tootin'! After all, I'm the one inviting. So sit down, stay awhile.

Boy howdy, do I love mah sake! An' buddy, I gotta say, ya
shore do know yer baseball. Man, don't that beat all!
Haven't talked like thish with someone in a long while!
You know... Wouldn't it be good to take a little breather?
Seriously, are you gonna be okay? You should probably call it a day.
Shut your face! You don't tell me what to do.
You criticizin' my lifestyle? Eh!? I ushed to be the ace of our company team! I don't "take breathers" on baseball, and I ain't gonna "call it a day"! *hic*
What the heck? I didn't say "quit baseball," I was talking about the sake.
Shurrup! You quit your yapping already! Tell ya what, punk-o, we settle thish over basebaw.
Settle this with baseball? ...That is what you said, right?
Yesh! You're telling me to quit basebaw! Then, you beat me and show me I'm done. You do that and I'll quit basheball, bam, cold turkey.
No, listen, I didn't say anything like that. Just lay off the sake, man!
Wouldja listen to yourshelf blather? *hic* Okay, okay, if you win, I give up this sake inshtead of baseball. Happy?
Gonna throw only five pitshes! You hit one homer off me, you win. How's that sound?
Hey, isn't that kinda unfair to me? I mean, I did get a little wasted myself...
Hush! Hush, I say! To the mound!
(Oh well. Better humor the guy. Sake's got me feeling a little shaky on my feet, but I'll just make the best of it.)
*sniffle* This can't be! That was my best pitching! Ahaaaaaaugh...
No need to cry, man. That was some pitching, especially seeing how drunk you are.
Hey, wake up!
Oh, geez. I'm sorry, my friend. When I get deep in the cups, I always get deep in the sleep. It's quite the phenomenon.
No, seriously, I must apologize. This is for keeping me out of trouble. Take it, why don't ya?
Hope you'll put this behind us and join me for a drink again!
No... I'm pretty sure I'll pass.
Ahahaha! I won, I won! I don't have to quit drinking after all!
Damn, when I'm this drunk, I can't swing worth beans.
Hah! Excuses! All excuses! If you want to prove me wrong, you'll have to beat me. I'm up for your challenge anytime! Ahaha!

I hereby challenge this batting center! The greatest of the
greats who train here should announce themself now!
Oh, he's back! It's the batting center challenger!
Ah, you're the shameful sport I struck down before. You wish to be humiliated again, I take it?
Hmph. It'll be different this time.

Oh? How amusing! Fine. Then I shall stomp you once again.
For the glory of the batting center sign!
The rules are the same. I will throw five pitches. If you can hit even one, you will emerge triumphant.
But if you miss them all, or I peg you with a beanball, victory will be mine.
Without further ado... Let the duel commence!
Hey, do you know anything about this batting center challenger?
What, you didn't hear? He's basically the batting center equivalent of a dojo breaker⑬one of those martial arts experts who goes around challenging dojo masters.
How the heck does that work?
From what I gather, he goes around to batting centers and challenges their best batters to a five-pitch duel.
If a batter loses or refuses the challenge, the guy takes the batting center's sign as his trophy.
Wow. Sounds nuts.
I hereby challenge this batting center!
Speak of the devil...
Could it be!?
Indeed it is! For I am none other than the batting center challenger feared throughout Kineicho!
The most supreme slugger of this here baseball-whacking establishment should announce himself now!
Well? No one? Yellow-bellied cowards! Then I shall take this batting center's sign as my own!
Hey! Over here! This guy's the best slugger you'll ever see!
Hey, don't just volunteer me!
It'll be fiiiine! Plus, the whole world wants to see this showdown just as much as I do!
You conniving little...
Ah, so it is you! Fwahaha! Then accept my challenge! Or else... I will stalk you for the rest of your life!
That is gross, and that is weird. But I'll do it. Happy now?

Very. I prefer to challenge men of reason anyway. Well then.
This is how our showdown will be. I shall throw a total of
five pitches. Hit even one and you will be triumphant.
But if you miss them all, or I hit you with a beanball, then victory is mine.
